stem: Which feature is characteristic of a normal thymus on a paediatric chest X-ray?

options.text: Significant mass effect on the trachea
Uniform soft tissue density with sharply demarcated borders
Visibility only in children older than 5 years
Complete symmetry on both sides of the mediastinum

explanation: Uniform soft tissue density with sharply demarcated borders is characteristic of a normal thymus on a paediatric chest X-ray. It may also appear triangular or show a sail sign, but it should not cause mass effect.

optionExplanations.A: Incorrect because a normal thymus does not usually produce significant tracheal mass effect.
optionExplanations.B: Correct because a normal thymus has a uniform soft tissue density with sharply demarcated borders on chest X-ray.
optionExplanations.C: Incorrect because the thymus is commonly visible in younger children, not only after 5 years of age.
optionExplanations.D: Incorrect because the thymus is not always perfectly symmetrical and may have a unilateral or triangular appearance.
optionExplanations.E: Incorrect because calcified, irregular margins are not features of a normal thymus.

source.hint: Recall the 'sail sign' and its impact on neighboring airways.
